title: Towers
statementMd:
As you know, all the kids in Berland love playing with cubes. Little Petya has $*n*$ towers consisting of cubes of the same size. Tower with number $*i*$ consists of $*a*_{*i*}$ cubes stacked one on top of the other. Petya defines the *instability* of a set of towers as a value equal to the difference between the heights of the highest and the lowest of the towers. For example, if Petya built five cube towers with heights (8, 3, 2, 6, 3), the instability of this set is equal to 6 (the highest tower has height 8, the lowest one has height 2).

The boy wants the instability of his set of towers to be as low as possible. All he can do is to perform the following operation several times: take the top cube from some tower and put it on top of some other tower of his set. Please note that Petya would never put the cube on the same tower from which it was removed because he thinks it's a waste of time.

Before going to school, the boy will have time to perform no more than $*k*$ such operations. Petya does not want to be late for class, so you have to help him accomplish this task.

## Input

The first line contains two space-separated positive integers $*n*$ and $*k*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$, $1 ≤ *k* ≤ 1000$) — the number of towers in the given set and the maximum number of operations Petya can perform. The second line contains $*n*$ space-separated positive integers $*a*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{4}$) — the towers' initial heights.

## Output

In the first line print two space-separated non-negative integers $*s*$ and $*m*$ ($*m* ≤ *k*$). The first number is the value of the minimum possible instability that can be obtained after performing at most $*k*$ operations, the second number is the number of operations needed for that.

In the next $*m*$ lines print the description of each operation as two positive integers $*i*$ and $*j*$, each of them lies within limits from $1$ to $*n*$. They represent that Petya took the top cube from the $*i*$-th tower and put in on the $*j*$-th one ($*i* ≠ *j*$). Note that in the process of performing operations the heights of some towers can become equal to zero.

If there are multiple correct sequences at which the minimum possible instability is achieved, you are allowed to print any of them.

## Note

In the first sample you need to move the cubes two times, from the second tower to the third one and from the second one to the first one. Then the heights of the towers are all the same and equal to 6.
statementZhMd:
如你所知，Berland 的所有孩子都喜欢玩方块。小 Petya 有 $*n*$ 座由大小相同的方块组成的塔。编号为 $*i*$ 的塔由一个接一个堆叠起来的 $*a*_{*i*}$ 个方块组成。Petya 将一组塔的*不稳定度*定义为最高塔与最低塔的高度之差。例如，如果 Petya 建造了五座高度分别为 (8, 3, 2, 6, 3) 的方块塔，那么这组塔的不稳定度为 6（最高的塔高度为 8，最低的塔高度为 2）。

男孩希望使他的塔组的不稳定度尽可能小。他能做的只有执行以下操作若干次：从某座塔的顶部取下一个方块，并将其放到他这组塔中的另一座塔的顶部。请注意，Petya 绝不会将方块放回取下它的同一座塔，因为他认为这样是在浪费时间。

在去学校之前，男孩至多有时间执行 $*k*$ 次操作。Petya 不想上课迟到，所以请你帮助他完成这项任务。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个用空格分隔的正整数 $*n*$ 和 $*k*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$，$1 ≤ *k* ≤ 1000$）——给定塔的数量以及 Petya 最多可以执行的操作次数。第二行包含 $*n*$ 个用空格分隔的正整数 $*a*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{4}$）——各座塔的初始高度。

## 输出格式

第一行输出两个用空格分隔的非负整数 $*s*$ 和 $*m*$（$*m* ≤ *k*$）。第一个数是执行至多 $*k*$ 次操作后能够得到的最小不稳定度，第二个数是达到该不稳定度所需的操作次数。

接下来的 $*m*$ 行输出每次操作的描述，每次包含两个正整数 $*i*$ 和 $*j*$，它们都在 $1$ 到 $*n*$ 的范围内。它们表示 Petya 从第 $*i*$ 座塔的顶部取下一个方块，并将其放到第 $*j*$ 座塔的顶部（$*i* ≠ *j*$）。注意，在执行操作的过程中，某些塔的高度可能会变为零。

如果存在多组能够达到最小可能不稳定度的正确操作序列，你可以输出其中任意一组。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，你需要移动两次方块：从第二座塔移动到第三座塔，再从第二座塔移动到第一座塔。这样所有塔的高度都相同，均为 6。
